Research questions, to be listed exactly as worded: RQ1 (verbatim): How has peer-reviewed research on technological innovation for the energy transition in Colombia evolved between 2015 and 2025 in volume, venues, institutions, collaboration networks and thematic clusters? PICOC: population Peer-reviewed studies on Colombia's energy system; intervention Technological advances and innovation for the energy transition; comparison Over time (2015-2025) and across thematic clusters; outcomes Publication trends, key authors and institutions, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence clusters, under-explored areas; context Colombia, national scope. RQ2 (verbatim): Which energy-transition technologies (non-conventional renewables, energy efficiency, storage, smart grids, microgrids, low-carbon fuels and hydrogen) have been studied for Colombia, by what methods, and what technical, economic and environmental outcomes do the studies report? PICOC: population Colombian energy supply and demand sectors (power, industry, buildings, transport, non-interconnected zones); intervention Deployment, design, modelling or assessment of energy-transition technologies; comparison Conventional fossil-based or incumbent alternatives, or between technologies, where reported; outcomes Technical performance, cost, emissions reduction, reliability and energy access; context Colombia, including the National Interconnected System (SIN) and the non-interconnected zones (ZNI). RQ3 (verbatim): What barriers and enablers, including policy, regulation, finance and institutions, do the studies identify for the adoption of technological innovation in Colombia's energy transition? PICOC: population Actors and institutions of Colombia's energy sector (government, regulators, utilities, industry, communities); intervention Policy instruments, regulatory frameworks (e.g., Law 1715 of 2014, Law 2099 of 2021), financing and innovation-system mechanisms; comparison Across technologies and, where reported, against other Latin American countries; outcomes Reported barriers, enablers and their effects on adoption; context Colombia. RQ4 (verbatim): What social, environmental and territorial impacts and conflicts are associated with the implementation of energy-transition technologies in Colombia? PICOC: population Communities and territories hosting or served by energy-transition projects (e.g., La Guajira, ZNI); intervention Implementation of renewable, efficiency or grid projects; comparison Not applicable; outcomes Socio-environmental impacts, conflicts, acceptance, energy justice and access; context Colombia. Contributions, one per research question in the same order: (1) a scientometric map of the field (RQ1); (2) a comparison of technologies, methods and reported technical, economic and environmental outcomes across six technology groups (RQ2); (3) a classification of barriers and enablers into the eight open-problem classes of the background (RQ3); (4) a synthesis of social, environmental and territorial impacts and conflicts, with the open challenges and research gaps they leave (RQ4).

Comparison of the existing reviews obtained in full text with this review's protocol: each of them covers either a single technology or topic (isolated microgrids, energy communities, energy financing, energy efficiency), a different geography (global clean energy research; Latin America), or a corpus closed before 2023; none combines a PRISMA 2020 systematic search of peer-reviewed literature on all energy-transition technologies for Colombia over 2015-2025 with a scientometric analysis and a comparative synthesis of outcomes, barriers, enablers and impacts, which this review does.
A scoping search of OpenAlex for works of type review on the review topic, run on 2026-11-17, returned 154 review records (openalex (type:review)).
